Counsel for Applicant :- Arun Kumar Pandey,Saurabh Pandey Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Lavania,J.
1. Counter and rejoinder affidavits are taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

The present application has been filed on behalf of the applicant seeking bail in Case Crime No.
0270 of 2023, under Sections-498A, 323, 504, 506, 427, 120B, 376D, 377, 392, 342 IPC and Section- 3/4 DP Act, P.S.- Motigarpur, District- Sultanpur.

entities.text: Karan Pandey vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While pressing the instant application, learned counsel for the applicant submitted that theapplicant is innocent and he has falsely been implicated in the present case.

5. It is further stated that the on account of matrimonial discord, the informant/victim lodged the FIR against all family members of the applicant making bald and baseless allegations so as to attract offence under Sections- 498A, 323, 504, 506, 427, 120B, 376D, 377, 392, 342 IPC and Section- 3/4 DP Act.

It is stated that lodging of FIR by the informant in such a manner in matrimonial disputes has been deprecated by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Geeta Mehrotra and others vs. State of U.P. and others reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741 and Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599.
6.

entities.text: Geeta Mehrotra and others vs. State of U.P. and others reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also stated that the story narrated in the FIR is completely bogus and improbable in view of the fact that blood relatives committed rape with the informant/victim.
7. It is further stated that there is no medical evidence available with the prosecution to support the allegations made in the FIR.

8. It is further stated that the FIR was lodged after huge delay of about 2 months and 8 days and from this delay, it can be inferred that with due consultation, the FIR was lodged making bald and baseless allegations against entire family members including the applicant.
9.

It is also stated that the dispute can be settled amicably and for this, an effort was also made by the father of the applicant by preferring an application dated 18.10.2023 but before the District Level Mediation and Conciliation Centre, the informant/victim avoided the proceedings and accordingly, the matter could not be settled and if the applicant is released on bail, he would try his best to settle the dispute amicably by involving respectable persons of the society.
Prayer is to grant bail to the applicant.
10. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer of the applicant, however, he could not dispute the above contentions made by the applicant's counsel.

11. Considering the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A.
and going through the contents of the application, F.I.R., as well as other relevant documents as also taking note of the fact that the applicant is having no criminal history and above referred judgments and without going into the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that the application has substance and it is accordingly, allowed.

12. Let theapplicant- Karan Pandey be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing personal bond of Rs. 25,000/- and two reliable sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions :-
(i) Theapplicant will cooperate with the prosecution during trial.
(ii) Theapplicant will not tamper with the evidence during trial.

entities.text: Karan Pandey vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) Theapplicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness(es).
(iv) Theapplicant shall not commit an offence.

(v) Theapplicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(vi) Theapplicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through counsel.
(vii) Theapplicant will not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.

(viii) Theapplicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
13.
In case of default of above conditions it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

14. As this order relates to enlargement of the applicant on bail, it is clarified that observations made in this order shall have no bearing on the merits of the case and the trial court shall not be influenced by any observation made in this order.
